item.title: International arrest warrant issued for former Steward Healthcare CEO Ralph de la Torre
item.description: Maltese authorities have issued an international arrest warrant for Ralph de la Torre, the former Steward Health Care chief who has not appeared in Malta to face charges arising from the magisterial inquiry into the hospitals concession. The Constitutional Court dismissed his attempt to suspend or stop the criminal proceedings before they had begun. Court hearings were told that correspondence was ongoing with the US embassy and that de la Torre's lawyer had held talks with the Attorney General's office about him coming to Malta voluntarily; he was charged in May 2024 and has been a no-show at four sittings since.
item.content:encoded:

Sources: Times of Malta

item.title: Government reiterates pledge to introduce five days of family violence leave
item.description: Equality and Civil Rights Minister Rosianne Cutajar said the government "remains committed" to introducing five days of family violence leave for victims of domestic violence, one of the Labour Party's electoral pledges, but gave no timeframe. Speaking at a conference on violence against women and the world of work, she said victims should not have to choose between their safety and their job, and that employment provides stability and economic independence during the process of rebuilding a life.

item.title: Birkirkara council insists civic centre has no room for police station
item.description: The Birkirkara local council has called an urgent meeting over the police station issue, following minister Glenn Bedingfield's claim that the council was lobbying for a new station in the civic centre. The council says the civic centre is fully utilised and cannot host a police station, and a statement was issued by mayor Desirei Grech and executive secretary Christine Jo Mansue. Malta Today reported the same position on the matter.

item.title: Ten new social housing apartments to be built in Paola
item.description: Two social housing projects in Paola will deliver ten new apartments through a combined investment of around €903,000, developed by Housing Projects Solutions Ltd. The Triq ix-Xewk project covers five one-bedroom apartments with excavation due to finish next week and completion expected by mid-July 2027; the Triq Imbroll project, already at third-floor level, is expected to finish by the end of January 2027. Housing Minister Owen Bonnici visited the works.

item.title: Malta could become Mediterranean hub for tourism safety
item.description: Malta could become a hub for cooperation on best practices in visitor safety following initiatives discussed at the 11th Mediterranean Tourism Forum, organised by the Mediterranean Tourism Foundation with around 1,500 participants and four action labs. One proposal being explored is MEDREADY, alongside the AI Hotel Blueprint. Tourism Minister Jo Etienne Abela said Malta is positioning itself as a leader in the region on tourism safety.

item.title: Food safety warning over undeclared mustard in organic soba noodles
item.description: The Food Safety Authority has warned consumers allergic to mustard to avoid a batch of organic soba noodles because it contains undeclared traces of mustard. The product is the Australian brand Hakubaku, best before date 1/06/2028, lot number 12.6B. The authority said the product must not be consumed by persons who are allergic or intolerant to mustard.

item.title: Bail denied for man accused of trafficking crack cocaine
item.description: A 28-year-old man from Żejtun was remanded in custody on Friday after pleading not guilty to seven charges tied to cocaine trafficking, conspiracy to traffic drugs and possession of weapons. The case was among the court business reported on the day, alongside separate proceedings in which a mother and son were remanded over an alleged organised crime network.

item.title: Police investigating altercation at Sports Direct outlet in Qormi
item.description: Video footage of an altercation between a customer and staff at the Sports Direct outlet in Qormi during Black Friday circulated on social media, showing a punch being thrown. Hudson Group, which operates the store, said it was aware of an incident involving a group of individuals and that police were called and are speaking to those concerned. Police confirmed they were called to the scene at around 2pm and a police report has been filed.

item.title: Capsized Malta-flagged diesel ship to be towed to Spanish port of Cartagena
item.description: The Malta-flagged diesel carrier Med Emre, carrying 7,000 tonnes of fuel, will be towed to the Spanish port of Cartagena, the transport ministry said. The vessel overturned early on Thursday off Ibiza, killing its chief engineer, according to its owner YMN Tankers. The fuel has been contained and the ship stabilised in open waters, and environmental groups have flagged risks to the area's flora, fauna and fisheries.
